# Refusals
Every rule that refuses a job on the job path, defined once in `src/ct/refusals.py`. A refused job's result carries the code, shown as its last row. Each rule says what it protects, so it can be questioned against the app's goals. Operational errors (a step that failed) are not listed here.

## Security

### `job.id.mismatch`: The job file's id does not match its name

- **Text:** id missing or does not match filename
- **Protects:** Stops a job file from claiming to be a different job than its file name, so an approval or result cannot be attached to the wrong one.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Send the job again with ct-run submit.

### `job.expired`: The job is too old to run

- **Text:** job expired: it is more than {hours} old when the worker looked at it, so it is not run; send it again
- **Protects:** Replay protection: a job file that was captured earlier cannot be run again later by whoever holds it.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** the worker's max_age_s (default 24 hours)
- **What to do:** Send the job again with ct-run submit.

### `job.created.future`: The job claims to be from the future

- **Text:** job timestamp is in the future
- **Protects:** A job dated in the future would stay valid longer than the age limit allows.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Check this computer's clock, then send the job again with ct-run submit.

### `job.class.unknown`: The job names a class the worker does not have

- **Text:** class not in installed registry: {name!r}
- **Protects:** Only classes the owner installed may run: a job can never name a command of its own, except a profile run, which needs approval.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** List what the worker offers with ct-run classes.

### `param.enum`: A parameter is not one of the allowed values

- **Text:** {name}: must be one of {options}
- **Protects:** A parameter that must be one of a fixed list can never carry anything else into the command.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** See the allowed values with ct-run classes.

### `param.int`: A number parameter is out of range

- **Text:** {name}: must be an integer in [{low}, {high}]
- **Protects:** A numeric parameter stays inside the range the class declares.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** See the allowed range with ct-run classes.

### `param.regex`: A parameter does not match its allowed pattern

- **Text:** {name}: does not match the allowed pattern
- **Protects:** A text parameter must match the pattern the class declares, so it cannot carry extra arguments or shell text into the command.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** See the allowed pattern with ct-run classes.

### `param.policy`: A parameter matches a deny rule

- **Text:** not allowed: {reason}
- **Protects:** The owner's deny rules (patterns that must never reach a command) apply to every parameter.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** the registry's policy: deny_params
- **What to do:** Change the value, or review the rule in your registry (ct-admin class).

### `files.name.path`: A file name could leave the job's folder

- **Text:** bad file name: {name!r} ({reason})
- **Protects:** Keeps a file inside the job's work folder: the name must be a relative path with no '..', empty part, control character or backslash, and a sane length. Nothing else about a name is checked: an earlier character list refused names like helper@.service.in and protected nothing.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Rename the file, or leave it out with --include on ct-run submit.

### `profile.command.denied`: The command is not allowed in a profile run

- **Text:** {program} is not allowed in a profile run
- **Protects:** A profile run is an arbitrary command, so privilege tools are refused outright whatever else is allowed.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** the registry's policy: deny_commands

### `profile.command.path_invalid`: The command's path is not an absolute executable

- **Text:** a command with a path must be an absolute path to an executable
- **Protects:** A command with a path must be one exact, absolute, executable file, never a relative path the job could place.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Give the full path, or the command's name.

### `job.action.missing`: The class's root-level action is missing

- **Text:** the class's action is not in the installed registry
- **Protects:** A root-level class must point at an action in the root-owned registry, or it would run nothing it could be checked against.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Reinstall the registry with ct-admin apply.

### `job.root.params_only`: A root-level job carries more than parameters

- **Text:** a root-level job takes parameters only
- **Protects:** A root-level job may carry only typed parameters: no files and no prompt can reach something that runs as root.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable

### `files.held.secret_name`: A file that usually holds a secret was held back

- **Text:** {name!r} was held back: its name is one that usually holds a secret
- **Protects:** Protects the person from sending a credential to a worker by accident: a file whose name conventionally holds a secret (.env, *.pem, id_rsa, .npmrc ...) is held back unless an --include names it exactly. A wildcard never sends one.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** the list of names in ct.client.submit (SECRET_NAMES), not configurable yet
- **What to do:** Send it anyway by naming it: --include 'PATH' on ct-run submit.

### `files.warn.secret_content`: A file being sent looks like it contains a secret

- **Text:** {name!r} contains text that looks like a private key or an API token
- **Protects:** Tells the person that a file being sent contains text shaped like a private key or an API token. It is only a warning, not a hold: source and test files often hold examples (23 of this project's own 283 files match).
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** If it is real, leave the file out with --include on ct-run submit.

## Format

### `job.id.invalid`: The job id is not allowed

- **Text:** bad job id
- **Protects:** Keeps job ids plain so they are safe as file names and in logs.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Send the job again with ct-run submit, which makes a valid id.

### `job.json.invalid`: The job file is not valid JSON

- **Text:** job file is not valid JSON
- **Protects:** A job that is not readable data cannot be checked, so it is never run.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Send the job again with ct-run submit.

### `job.created.invalid`: The job has no readable creation time

- **Text:** missing or invalid 'created' timestamp
- **Protects:** The age check (replay protection) needs the job's own creation time.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Send the job again with ct-run submit, which writes it.

### `job.created.no_timezone`: The job's creation time has no timezone

- **Text:** 'created' needs a timezone (use UTC, e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z)
- **Protects:** A creation time without a timezone cannot be compared with the worker's clock.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Send the job again with ct-run submit, which writes it in UTC.

### `job.params.not_object`: The job's parameters are not an object

- **Text:** params must be an object
- **Protects:** Parameters must be named values so each one can be checked against its declared type.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Give each parameter as -p name=value on ct-run submit.

### `job.invalid`: The job did not pass a check

- **Text:** {detail}
- **Protects:** A catch-all for a check that has not been given its own entry yet (these are being moved into the catalog).
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable

### `param.untyped`: A class parameter has no type

- **Text:** {name}: registry spec has no type
- **Protects:** A class parameter with no declared type cannot be checked, so it is refused rather than passed through.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Give the parameter a type in the class, with ct-admin class.

### `param.unknown`: The job has a parameter the class does not declare

- **Text:** unknown params: {names}
- **Protects:** A parameter the class did not declare is never passed on.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** See the declared parameters with ct-run classes.

### `param.missing`: A required parameter is missing

- **Text:** missing param: {name}
- **Protects:** A required parameter that is absent would leave a placeholder in the command.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Give it as -p {name}=value on ct-run submit.

### `template.undeclared`: The class's command uses an undeclared parameter

- **Text:** template uses undeclared param {name}
- **Protects:** A class whose command template names a parameter it never declared is a mistake in the class, so it is refused.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Correct the class with ct-admin class.

### `files.unreadable`: A file could not be read

- **Text:** file {name!r} could not be read: {reason}
- **Protects:** A file that cannot be read cannot be sent, and the person is told which one and why, not left to find a missing file in the result.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Run ls -l on the file to see its permissions, then run the same command again.

### `profile.packages.path`: A command with packages must be given by name

- **Text:** with packages, give the command by name (the program comes from the throwaway folder)
- **Protects:** With packages the program comes from the throwaway folder, so a path to a program on the worker would be ambiguous.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Give the command by name, without a path, on ct-run offload profile.

### `profile.field.invalid`: A description field is missing or too long

- **Text:** {field}: {rule}
- **Protects:** The description fields are what the person who approves reads, so they must be present and short enough to read.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** a profile run that needs approval
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Fill it in with the matching option on ct-run offload profile.

### `profile.estimate.required`: An estimate is missing

- **Text:** {field}: required (your honest estimate, as a number)
- **Protects:** The estimates are compared with what the run measured, so the worker's limits and the verdict can be set from them.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Give it with the matching option on ct-run offload profile.

### `job.profile.params`: A profile run was given parameters

- **Text:** profile-run takes argv, not params
- **Protects:** A profile run is one exact command, not a class with parameters.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Give the command after a double dash on ct-run offload profile.

### `job.kind.unknown`: The class is of an unknown kind

- **Text:** unknown kind {kind!r}
- **Protects:** A class of a kind this worker does not know cannot be run safely.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Update the worker with ct-admin apply.

## Limit

### `files.too_many`: Too many files are attached

- **Text:** files must be an object with at most {limit} entries
- **Protects:** Bounds how much one job asks of the worker and of the channel that carries it.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** the transport (these limits were written for GitHub)
- **Configured:** the worker's registry: limits.files.max_count (moving to the transport config)
- **What to do:** Attach fewer files with --include on ct-run submit.

### `files.not_text`: A file is not text

- **Text:** file {name!r} is not text, so it cannot be sent in a job
- **Protects:** A job file carries file contents as text, so a file that is not text cannot be sent yet. It is reported and never dropped silently; archive transfer is a later design.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** the carrier (text inside the job file)
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Leave it out with --include on ct-run submit.

### `files.too_big`: A file is too big

- **Text:** file {name!r}: content must be text under {limit} KB
- **Protects:** Bounds one file's size so a single file cannot fill the job file.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** the transport (written for GitHub)
- **Configured:** the worker's registry: limits.files.max_file_kb (moving to the transport config)
- **What to do:** Leave the file out with --include on ct-run submit.

### `files.total_too_big`: The attached files are too big together

- **Text:** files total over {limit} KB
- **Protects:** Bounds the whole job's size for the channel that carries it.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** the transport (written for GitHub)
- **Configured:** the worker's registry: limits.files.max_total_kb (moving to the transport config)
- **What to do:** Attach only the files the command needs with --include on ct-run submit.

### `profile.argv.shape`: The command is not a list of 1 to 40 words

- **Text:** argv must be a list of 1-40 non-empty strings
- **Protects:** A command is a short list of plain words, so it can be shown whole to the person who approves it and cannot hide NUL bytes.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Give the command after a double dash on ct-run offload profile.

### `profile.estimate.range`: An estimate is out of range

- **Text:** {field}: must be a number from 0 to 1000000
- **Protects:** An estimate must be a plausible number so a typo cannot set an absurd limit.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Give a number with the matching option on ct-run offload profile.

### `profile.flags.invalid`: The flag explanations are not usable

- **Text:** flags must map each flag to a short explanation (at most 20)
- **Protects:** The flag explanations are shown on the approval screen, which has room for a few short ones.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** a profile run that needs approval
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Shorten them with --flag on ct-run offload profile.

### `profile.timeout.range`: The time limit is out of range

- **Text:** timeout_s must be an integer from 10 to {cap}
- **Protects:** A profile run's time limit stays between a floor that lets it start and the cap the owner set.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** the class's max_timeout_s
- **What to do:** Give a value in range with --timeout on ct-run offload profile.

### `placement.capacity.in_flight`: Too many jobs are already running

- **Text:** Sending {adding} more would pass limits.max_in_flight. In flight now: {where}.
- **Protects:** Bounds how many jobs this computer has running across all workers at once.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** your configuration: [limits] max_in_flight (0 removes it)
- **What to do:** Wait for some to finish: ct-run jobs shows them. Or raise the cap in your configuration under [limits]: max_in_flight = <number> (0 removes it).

### `job.prompt.length`: The prompt has the wrong length

- **Text:** prompt must be 1-8000 characters
- **Protects:** Bounds what one AI job can spend; the cap is a fixed number today and should become a setting per class.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** the class kind: claude
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Shorten the prompt, or attach the text as a file.

## Placement

### `profile.command.not_installed`: The worker does not have that command

- **Text:** {program!r} is not installed on the worker (looked in {looked}); if a package provides it, list the package (packages: ['apt:<name>'])
- **Protects:** The worker can only run what it has; it says so instead of failing in the middle of the run.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Name the package with --package on ct-run offload profile.

### `placement.unreachable`: A worker cannot be reached

- **Text:** cannot be reached now ({reason})
- **Protects:** A worker that cannot be reached cannot be asked anything, so nothing else about it can be known: this reason stands alone.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Check it with ct-admin check.

### `placement.no_state`: A worker has published no state

- **Text:** has published no state (an older release, or not set up yet), so nothing can be said about it
- **Protects:** A worker that has published no state cannot be described, so no job is placed on it blind.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Update it with ct-admin apply.

### `placement.locked`: A worker is locked

- **Text:** is LOCKED (a security lockdown): unlock it after you have looked
- **Protects:** The worker locked itself after a security event and runs nothing until the owner has looked.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Look at what happened with ct-admin quarantine, then run ct-admin unlock.

### `placement.isolation_off`: A worker's job isolation is off

- **Text:** has its job isolation OFF
- **Protects:** A job runs only where its isolation is on.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** See why with ct-admin status.

### `placement.reserved`: A worker is reserved for other work

- **Text:** is reserved for {classes}
- **Protects:** The owner reserved this worker for certain classes, and it takes nothing else.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** ct-admin workers use WORKER --command CLASS
- **What to do:** Release it with ct-admin workers use WORKER --clear.

### `placement.class_missing`: A worker does not offer the class

- **Text:** does not offer the class {cls}
- **Protects:** A worker can only run the classes its registry has.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** See which workers offer it with ct-run classes.

### `placement.tools.full_isolation`: A worker's isolation cannot show the tool folders

- **Text:** is in full isolation, so it cannot show the tool folders {cls} needs
- **Protects:** A class that needs the tool folders already on a worker runs only where the owner allowed that.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Allow the tool folders with ct-admin class.

### `placement.tools.not_allowed`: A worker does not allow the tool folder

- **Text:** does not allow the tool folder {folder} that {cls} needs
- **Protects:** A class that needs a tool folder runs only where the owner allowed that folder.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Allow the folder with ct-admin class.

### `placement.connection`: A worker is reached over a connection the class does not allow

- **Text:** is reached over {listens}, and {cls} is limited to {allowed}
- **Protects:** The owner limited this class to some kinds of connection.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** the transport
- **Configured:** ct-admin class
- **What to do:** See the limits with ct-admin class.

### `placement.ai.no_signin`: A worker has no AI sign-in

- **Text:** has no Claude sign-in
- **Protects:** An AI class runs only where the AI tool is signed in.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** the class kind: claude
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Sign it in with ct-setup install --worker NAME.

### `placement.ai.no_tool`: A worker has no AI tool

- **Text:** has no Claude tool installed
- **Protects:** An AI class runs only where its tool is installed.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** the class kind: claude
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Install it with ct-setup install --worker NAME.

### `placement.ai.paused`: A worker paused AI jobs for today

- **Text:** has paused Claude jobs for today (its daily limit)
- **Protects:** An AI worker stops taking AI jobs for the day when its limit is reached, so the person's usage is bounded.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** the class kind: claude
- **Configured:** the worker's daily limits
- **What to do:** See its usage with ct-admin status.

### `placement.none_available`: No worker can take this job right now

- **Text:** Each one, and why it cannot:
- **Protects:** A job with no worker that can take it is not sent: the person is told why for each worker.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Compare the workers with ct-admin workers.

### `placement.unknown_worker`: There is no such worker

- **Text:** Workers are the main one and those in ct-admin workers.
- **Protects:** A job sent to a named worker needs the name to be one of the person's workers.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** List your workers with ct-admin workers.

### `placement.pin.unknown_worker`: The folder file sends jobs to a worker that is not yours

- **Text:** The worker named in the file is not one of your workers.
- **Protects:** A folder's .tenta.toml that names a worker which is not the person's would send jobs nowhere.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Send this folder's jobs to one of your workers: ct-run use WORKER ct-run use --clear

### `placement.locked.submit`: The worker is locked, so this job was not submitted

- **Text:** It locked itself after a security event and runs nothing until you have reviewed it.
- **Protects:** A worker that locked itself after a security event takes no new job, so nothing is sent to it.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** First look at what happened, then unlock it:

### `job.packages.plan`: The requested packages cannot be installed

- **Text:** {problems}
- **Protects:** The packages a job asks for must be installable here, or the job would start and fail.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Check the package names with ct-run offload profile.

## Policy

### `files.not_accepted`: The class does not take files

- **Text:** this job class does not accept files
- **Protects:** Only classes that were registered to take input files get any, so files cannot influence a command that was not made for them.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** the class: accepts_files
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** See which classes take files with ct-run classes.

### `files.name.hidden`: This kind of class takes no file whose name starts with a dot

- **Text:** a name may not start with a dot for this kind of class: {name!r}
- **Protects:** A class whose tool reads its settings from its working folder (an AI tool) must not get a settings file planted by a job, so such a class takes no name that starts with a dot.
- **Decided by:** worker
- **Depends on:** the class kind: claude (decided by the kind, never by a setting the person makes)
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Leave the file out with --include on ct-run submit.

### `files.incomplete`: Some files could not be sent

- **Text:** {count} could not be sent, so the job would run on an incomplete set of files
- **Protects:** A test or any job run on part of the files answers a question about something else, so the person decides whether to go on without the files that could not be sent.
- **Decided by:** client
- **Depends on:** nothing
- **Configured:** not configurable
- **What to do:** Make the files listed above sendable or leave them out with --include, then run the same command again. Or run the same command again with --send-incomplete to send the rest.
